subject: Polity
description: Supreme Court, High Courts, writs, judicial review

questions.stem: The Supreme Court of India was established on:
questions.explanation: SC of India — 26 January 1950, with the coming into force of the Constitution. Replaced the Federal Court (established 1937 under GoI Act 1935) and the Privy Council (London) as the apex court. First sat in the Chamber of Princes inside the Parliament House, now in its own building on Tilak Marg. replacing the Federal Court, 1937-1950.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The sanctioned STRENGTH of the Supreme Court (Chief Justice + other judges) is currently:
questions.explanation: SC (Number of Judges) Amendment Act, 2019 raised the strength to 34 (CJI + 33 judges). Originally 8 at inception, raised over the years. Judges retire at 65 (SC), 62 (HC).
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Match the WRIT with its PURPOSE. A. Habeas Corpus.  B. Mandamus.  C. Quo Warranto.  D. Certiorari. List-II: 1. To produce an illegally detained person.  2. To command a public authority to do its duty.  3. To question a person's authority to hold a public office.  4. To quash a lower court's/authority's order on jurisdictional grounds.
questions.explanation: 5 constitutional writs (Arts 32, 226): Habeas Corpus = 'have the body'; Mandamus = 'we command'; Quo Warranto = 'by what authority'; Certiorari = 'to be informed'; Prohibition (the 5th, not listed above) — prevents lower court from proceeding.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Under Article 32, writs can be issued by:
questions.explanation: Art 32 — Supreme Court (heart and soul of the Constitution, per Ambedkar) for enforcement of Fundamental Rights. Art 226 — High Courts have a WIDER jurisdiction (can issue writs for FR enforcement AND 'for any other purpose'). Both can issue habeas/mandamus/certiorari/prohibition/quo warranto.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The CHIEF JUSTICE of India is appointed by:

options.option_text: The President, on the collegium's recommendation

questions.explanation: CJI appointed by President (Art 124(2)). Since the Second Judges Case (1993) and Third Judges Case (1998), the SC Collegium (CJI + senior-most 4 SC judges) makes binding recommendations. Govt can send back once; if reiterated, must accept. NJAC struck down in 2015.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The RETIREMENT AGE of a Supreme Court judge is:
questions.explanation: SC judges — retire at 65. HC judges — 62 (raised from 60 in 1963 by 15th Amendment). SC/HC judges removed only through impeachment-like procedure under Art 124(4) — proved misbehaviour or incapacity, passed by both Houses with special majority.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The 'BASIC STRUCTURE' doctrine — limiting Parliament's amending power — was established in which case?
questions.explanation: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973) — 13-judge bench, 7-6 majority. Held that Parliament can amend the Constitution but cannot alter its 'basic structure'. List is illustrative (rule of law, judicial review, federalism, secularism, democracy, separation of powers, etc.), not exhaustive. Overruled Golak Nath.
